newsitem.title: USA: Edmark CEO resigns, citing health reasons.
newsitem.headline: Edmark CEO resigns, citing health reasons.

text.p: Edmark Corp., a maker of educational computer software for children, said Monday that its Chairman and Chief Executive officer Sally Narodick has resigned for health reasons.
The company said Donna Stanger, vice president for product development, will assume the duties of chief executive on an interim basis while the board of directors searches for a permanent CEO.
Frances Conley, a director of the company and principal of Roanoke Capital Ltd., will serve as chairman of the board.

"This has been a very difficult decision for me, but one that I feel is in the best interests of the company," said Narodick in statement. "I have been experiencing some stress-related health problems that are interfering with my ability to continue as Edmark's CEO."
Narodick, who said she had "great confidence" in Stanger, will remain on the board.
Narodick, 51, a former banker, joined Edmark in 1989 and rapidly transformed it from a producer of special-education materials to a company focused on multimedia software.

While the education market still accounts for 35 percent of the company's $32 million in annual revenues, increasingly Edmark has been aiming at the consumer market, where it faces increasingly stiff competition from the likes of Broderbund Software Inc. and Walt Disney Co.
Edmark, which was founded in 1970 and went public in 1985, also has been buffeted by pricing pressure that have cut into the company's profit margins, said John Taylor of Arcadia Investment Corp.
"I think Edmark is at a little bit of a crossroads here," he said. "The marketplace has turned pretty hostile to small publishers of edutainment software."
Edmark's stock has fluctuated widely from a peak of more than $50 in October 1995 to its close Monday at $12.50, down $1.50. The news was announced after the market closed.
